storylines.label: DeepSeek Pro
storylines.latest_title: Qwen 3.8 Flash Reduces Costs to One-Third of DeepSeek-V4-Flash

prior_narrative.tldr: A week of price-hike warnings ended with DeepSeek confirming V4 Pro on Aug 13 at sharply higher API prices and open-sourcing Harness, an MIT-licensed Claude Code rival, the same day. Harness drew broad developer pickup, added Claude Code and Codex as sub-agents by Aug 21, and V4-Flash-Vision-Exp shipped as DeepSeek's first multimodal model — then the Aug 23 weekend-surcharge rollback left cumulative peak prices still up 355%.
prior_narrative.whats_new: No patch or DeepSeek response has surfaced in the two days since QiAnXin disclosed a critical RCE flaw in Harness on Aug 25 — an Aug 26 analysis already pins V4 Pro's practical safety on that wrapper, not the model's guardrails.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Harness is now agent infrastructure — a plugin layer that schedules Claude Code and Codex as sub-agents — carrying a disclosed, unpatched RCE with no vendor response in the thread. V4 Pro's base price also stays well above pre-hike levels; the weekend rollback trimmed the surcharge, not the hike.

status.state: Unpatched RCE in Harness · price hike stands
status.reenable: no patch, CVE, or DeepSeek response yet
status.detail: V4 Pro shipped Aug 13 at sharply higher prices and DeepSeek ended the weekend surcharge Aug 23, but cumulative peak prices remain up 355%. Revenue reached $70M as of July, a tenfold jump from 2025, reported the same week the open security thread began: QiAnXin's Aug 25 RCE disclosure in Harness and the Aug 26 analysis tying V4 Pro's practical safety to it, with no follow-up since.

track.label: safety tied to the flaw, still unpatched

beats.headline: Price-hike reports build for over a week, and a hands-on already finds cracks in the "cheaper" pitch
beats.summary: Regional coverage flags a coming price increase for days before V4 Pro's launch makes it real. The New Stack's Aug 10 hands-on finds the "better and cheaper" pitch holds only partly; the-decoder.com still has DeepSeek beating Microsoft's MAI Code on price; finance.biggo.com clocks V4-Flash at $72, 33x cheaper than Kimi K3.

beats.headline: DeepSeek publicizes a dedicated team building agent tools to rival Claude Code
beats.summary: A Pi-founder claim that DeepSeek plus Pi already beats Claude Code opens the day; hours later Bloomberg is first to report DeepSeek forming a team aimed squarely at Anthropic's Claude Code, corroborated same-day by PYMNTS and repeated by briefs.co and TradingView into Aug 13 — hours before that team's tool ships.

beats.headline: A wave of Qwen 3.8 coverage and same-keyword noise rides the shared search cluster
beats.summary: Not part of the DeepSeek story: eleven Qwen 3.8 pieces, a Kimi-K3-vs-Claude-Opus study, a Simon Willison post on Claude Code's Auto Mode, and an unrelated "harness builder" project (Archon) that only shares the word "harness" — all riding the shared search cluster. Flagged for transparency, not narrative continuity.

beats.headline: A quiet OpenRouter build becomes DeepSeek's officially confirmed V4 Pro release, at sharply higher prices
beats.summary: Simon Willison spots the refreshed Pro model listed API-only with no announcement page; a day later Lufkin Daily News, Reuters, The Information, and Global Times confirm it as a deliberate release, with Nikkei Asia reporting sharply higher user prices and Yahoo Finance Singapore the raised V4 API rates.

beats.headline: DeepSeek open-sources Harness, a free Claude Code rival, and it draws fast, broad developer pickup
beats.summary: VentureBeat first reports Harness shipping alongside the pricier V4-Pro API; DeepSeek confirms V4 Pro leaving preview, and both go live on China's national supercomputing network by Aug 15. Fourteen more outlets pick up the "everything is a plugin" framing through Aug 17 — hands-on tests, an against-Claude-Cowork framing, and the formal v0.1 developer-preview release.

beats.headline: Harness ships a post-beta update adding multimodal input and sub-agent integration
beats.summary: Pandaily reports 14 changes in Harness's first post-beta update, including multimodal input and subagent upgrades; a day later, coverage details 3 weekly updates that integrate Claude Code and Codex as sub-agents, positioning Harness as a scheduling layer over other agent tools rather than a standalone rival.

beats.headline: Recap widens to a US-China AI-race frame, quantifies the hike, then pits V4 Pro's price and capability against Qwen 3.8 Max
beats.summary: Coverage widens: benchmark gains cited, the hike framed as a strategy shift and a US-China race, Forbes quantifies it at 14x the cheapest model, and TheSequence reviews it alongside GLM-5.3 and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. Willison's Artificial Analysis check puts Qwen 3.8 27B one point behind V4 Pro — DeepSeek's open-weight edge is thin. Memeburn reframes the hike against Qwen 3.8 Max.

beats.headline: DeepSeek ships V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, its first multimodal model pitched against Opus 4.8
beats.summary: Eight outlets corroborate the vision-capable model over two days — Seeking Alpha and Investing.com first, then Cryptonews ties it to reported IPO speculation, oodaloop and the-decoder frame it against Opus 4.8's agent-benchmark performance, and Tech in Asia confirms the vision-capable test build a day later with no new capability claims.

beats.headline: DeepSeek drops its weekend peak-pricing surcharge, then reports revenue reaching $70M, a tenfold jump
beats.summary: Bloomberg and a second outlet report DeepSeek ending the weekend peak-pricing surcharge for API users the same day a comparison piece puts cumulative peak-price increases at 355% since the original hike — an incremental de-escalation, not a reversal. Three days later, The Information reports the first hard business figure since the hike: revenue reached $70M as of July, a tenfold jump from 2025.

beats.headline: Harness carries a disclosed, unpatched RCE — and V4 Pro's safety is now argued to ride on it
beats.summary: QiAnXin discloses a critical, still-unpatched remote-code-execution flaw in Harness on Aug 25, the primary source behind the Aug 26 analysis tying V4 Pro's practical safety to the wrapper. Nothing has answered it since: no patch, CVE, or DeepSeek statement appears in the thread's remaining coverage.

open_questions: Has QiAnXin's Harness RCE flaw been assigned a CVE or fixed in a named version, and does DeepSeek dispute that V4 Pro's safety depends on it?
Is the Aug 24 "new multimodal model" a distinct release from V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, or delayed coverage of the same Aug 21 launch — what is its actual name and spec?
Now that Harness schedules Claude Code and Codex as sub-agents, does that change the RCE flaw's blast radius versus running Harness standalone?
Does V4 Pro's claimed "agent gains" reclaim the benchmark lead V4-Flash took in July, or does Flash remain the stronger agent option?
Forbes prices V4 Pro at 14x DeepSeek's cheapest model — is that still cheaper than Qwen 3.8 Max per token, or has DeepSeek lost its price edge to Alibaba?
Does the $70M revenue figure reflect post-hike pricing, or mostly pre-Aug-13 rates — how much of the jump is the price hike versus adoption growth?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Keep Harness and its Claude Code/Codex sub-agent integration off production credentials and untrusted input until a fixed version or CVE is published — QiAnXin's disclosure is 2 days old with no patch in sight. Re-price any DeepSeek plan against post-Aug-13 rates, not pre-hike numbers.
